proposed_features.description: The primary axis of the subject's body relative to the water surface or vertical axis, which distinguishes horizontal swimming from vertical falling.
The specific rhythmic or coordinated motion of the arms and legs, distinguishing the alternating arm cycle of one stroke from the simultaneous arm recovery of another.
The position of the head relative to the water surface, which is a key differentiator between the two swimming styles shown.
The direction of the subject's movement through the space, distinguishing horizontal progression from vertical descent.
The physical structure or location from which the action originates, distinguishing pool-based actions from high-altitude or natural rock formations.
The nature of the contact with the water, distinguishing continuous propulsion through the medium from a single impact event.
The temporal length of the primary action, distinguishing sustained rhythmic movement from a brief, instantaneous event.
The visibility of artificial lane dividers, which indicates a controlled swimming pool environment versus open water or natural settings.
The vertical distance of the subject from the water surface at the start of the action, distinguishing high-altitude jumps from surface-level swimming.
The straightness or curvature of the body, distinguishing the streamlined posture of a dive from the bent posture of a swimmer.
The temporal pattern of the movement, distinguishing the cyclic nature of swimming from the linear, non-repeating nature of a fall.
The general setting of the action, distinguishing artificial pool structures from natural geological features.
